angle: The combo sheet credits this deck with nineteen two-card infinites and the record signs exactly one, so the game you actually win is the grind that turns other people's counters into deathtouch bodies — and the thing that beats you is any permanent that isn't a creature.

teases: Mikaeus + Devoted Druid: four counter placements and one death every cycle, and not one mana in it
Six famous pairings stop dead at a single undying return — the altars are value, not a kill
Hapatra on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs: the card your opening seven never has to find
One permanent class answered out of five — the number that picks your bad matchups for you

departments.note: Hero art: Hapatra art_crop at full bleed. The dominant coverline is the one signed line in the issue; the kicker states the finding (one of nineteen), never a tier.
Generated table: five act headers, promises verbatim from issue_spec, tier legend and masthead trio in full.

departments.headline: SHE IS NEVER THE PROBLEM
departments.dek: Two mana, and the seeded runs put her on the battlefield on turn two in 9,970 games out of 10,000. That is the one card your opening seven never has to hunt — so spend all seven hunting the other one.
departments.body:
Begin with the exhibit everyone skips: the zone itself. Rule 903.4 seats Hapatra there before a card is drawn, and she may be cast from it any time you could cast a sorcery. She costs two. The seeded runs put her on the battlefield on turn two 9,970 times in 10,000, mean cast turn 2.007.

The holding inverts your mulligan. Your opening seven never has to hold her. All seven cards are free to hunt the thing the zone cannot promise — a repeatable way to put -1/-1 counters on a creature.

Now read the ladder above against this deck's ledger. Rule 903.8 adds {2} to every return trip: four the second time, six the third. Mean available mana is 4.71 on turn four and 6.15 on turn six. A second cast is on schedule. A third is a turn, not a tragedy.

So the court's spending advice is blunt. For Hapatra, pay the tax. Keep Heroic Intervention and the boots for Yawgmoth and Mikaeus — the pieces the zone does not hand back.

Colour identity is the clause with teeth. Rule 903.4 counts mana symbols in rules text and not only in costs, and black-green admits every -1/-1 counter card on this record while forbidding the counterspell outright.

Note what it does not forbid. Green owns artifact and enchantment removal, and this 99 carries none of it. That hole is a choice, not a legal constraint, and it belongs in your Rule 0 conversation stated plainly.

On the 21-damage clock, rule 903.10a, the record is short. Hapatra is an unevasive 2/2, and eleven connections against one defender is not a plan. The case file classifies her combat trigger as a bonus. The clock exists; it is not yours.

Coach's corner, and it is a strange seat. You are the only player with a permanent doing real work on turn two, and nobody is looking at you — visible and boring at the same time. Bank every turn that read buys you, and expect it revoked the first time one of your eleven Game Changers resolves.

pilot_tips.text: Send her into open mana on purpose — she is the only permanent in this 99 with a printed price for coming back.

captions.Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons: **THE EXCHANGE RATE:** she does not place -1/-1 counters at will. She pays you a 1/1 deathtouch Snake every time something else places one.
captions.Heroic Intervention: **SPEND PROTECTION HERE:** the command zone hands your commander back for {2}. It hands Yawgmoth and Mikaeus back for nothing at all.

departments.pull_quote: Your opening seven never has to find her. Spend all seven cards finding what she cannot do herself.

departments.headline: SHE'S A MINT, NOT A SOURCE
departments.dek: Every -1/-1 counter anyone places buys you a deathtouch body, and every body buys a card or a drain. The scarce half is the card that places the counters — so that is the half you go and get.

callouts.title: MINT THE BODY
callouts.text: Put a -1/-1 counter anywhere and Hapatra hands you a 1/1 deathtouch Snake. Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction and Serrated Arrows all do that for one mana or less.

callouts.title: CASH THE BODY
callouts.text: Skullclamp turns that Snake into two cards for {1}, and Deadly Dispute and Village Rites do it at instant speed. Your commander finds a payoff beside her in 67.2% of games at mean turn 3.62.

callouts.title: DRAIN THE TABLE
callouts.text: A converter that hits every seat is what turns the stream into a win. You hold one in 51.9% of games, and Obelisk Spider is the one to want — it drains on the counter, not on the death.

pilot_tips.text: Deploy the Spider last of your converters — it reads as a kill the moment it lands beside a repeatable source.
Clamp the Snake you were already about to sacrifice; the equip and the sacrifice are the same two cards.

captions.Yawgmoth, Thran Physician: **THE SCARCE HALF:** eight sacrifice outlets here cost no mana, and exactly one of them also places a counter. This is what the first tutor is for.
captions.Nest of Scarabs: **A SECOND MINT:** your placements make Insects as well as Snakes, so one sweeper pays twice. Deploy it before Black Sun's Zenith, never after.

departments.pull_quote: Hunt sources, not payoffs. The payoffs are six deep and the sources are two.

departments.headline: SIXTY-FOUR SPELLS, ONE JOB EACH
departments.dek: Sorted by the job, never the alphabet — because the only ranking that matters here is how close a card sits to a counter being placed. Three cards mint; everything else feeds them or spends what they make.

roster.role: The sources — the class that is two deep
The converters — a clock on every seat

cards: Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel

roster.role: The ceiling — one case file, eleven open questions
Protection, recursion and the odd jobs
The second jobs — lands that also do something
The colour — both, every time, and never tapped
The basics — seven Swamps, seven Forests

pilot_tips.text: Cast Toxic Deluge to survive and never to build — -X/-X places no counters, so Hapatra, Nest of Scarabs and Necroskitter all stay silent.
Feed Carrion Feeder Snakes and keep it away from anything you want dead — its own +1/+1 counters fight your removal.

captions.Necroskitter: **THE STEAL:** put counters on their board before you sweep it, not after. Every creature that dies wearing one comes back on your side.
captions.Bitterblossom: **THE REBUILD:** a body every upkeep for one life, from an enchantment no creature wrath can touch. It is a keep all by itself.

departments.headline: FOUR HANDS, ONE QUESTION
departments.dek: You keep the first seven 79.9% of the time and average 0.243 mulligans, so you can afford to be strict. Ask each of these hands one thing: does it reach a repeatable -1/-1 source?

hands.why: Three lands, a turn-one dork, the only free repeatable source in the 99 and two ways to cash what it makes. Your commander waits in the zone, so this hand is already holding the card the zone cannot promise.

A two-lander carries when a dork comes with it, and Demonic Tutor is any card you like. Keep Blowfly Infestation for what it reliably is — a counter source for the grind — and never as half of a kill nobody has signed.
Four lands, three converters, and nothing at all that places a counter. The simulation keeps this hand because its rule only counts lands; you are smarter than the simulation.

hands.verdict: SHIP — one land and a six-drop
hands.why: Mikaeus is your only six-drop and he places no counters himself. One land and a Petal will not get you there, and the rest of the hand is waiting on him.

pilot_tips.text: Keep Bitterblossom alone — one card that makes a body every upkeep and rebuilds through a wrath without any help.

captions.Blood Artist: **THE CLASSIC TRAP KEEP:** he is an exchange rate, and an exchange rate with nothing to exchange is a blank until you draw a source.

departments.headline: TWO BOARDS, NO HINTS
departments.dek: One turn-two question about which two-mana card goes first, and one turn-five choice between a famous loop and a checked one. Say your answer out loud before you read ours.

callouts.title: COUNT THE OPEN MANA
callouts.text: Both boards turn on what the seat with untapped lands can do to the card you are about to spend. Count it before you tap, not after.

callouts.title: ASK WHAT COMES BACK
callouts.text: One card in each hand has a printed price for returning and the rest are singletons you lose forever. That is usually most of the answer.

departments.pull_quote: An unadjudicated line is one you take with a spare body and a land still up — never the one you spend your pivot turn on.

departments.headline: INFINITE, EXCEPT THE MANA
departments.dek: The sheet claims nineteen two-card infinites in these colours. Four resolver passes under four adversarial reviews signed one of them — and told six others to sit down.

callouts.title: UNTAP FOR A COUNTER
callouts.text: Devoted Druid untaps by putting a -1/-1 counter on itself, and Hapatra mints a Snake off every placement. There is no tap symbol in that cost, so this loop never needs haste.

callouts.title: LET THE DRUID DIE
callouts.text: Enough counters and the Druid reaches zero toughness. Mikaeus gives it undying, so it comes straight back — a brand-new object wearing a +1/+1 counter.

callouts.title: ANNIHILATE AND GO AGAIN
callouts.text: The next -1/-1 counter cancels that +1/+1 as a state-based action, and undying is armed for the following pass. The record clocks the steady state at four counter placements and one death per cycle, for no mana at all.

callouts.title: TAKE THE GREEN ONCE
callouts.text: Three green on the first pass and none afterwards: the returned Druid has not been under your control since your turn began, so its tap ability is switched off. Count this loop as bodies and drain, never as ramp.

pilot_tips.text: Greaves restores the mana half of the loop, and its shroud then locks Hapatra and Yawgmoth out of targeting — move it off before you start placing counters.
With Mikaeus on the battlefield, an altar activation buys exactly one undying return: take the death trigger and never announce it as a kill.

captions.Mikaeus, the Unhallowed: **THE ANTHEM WITH A CATCH:** undying gives a creature back wearing a +1/+1 counter, and it will not return that body again until something strips it.
captions.Devoted Druid: **THE ONE PARTNER:** unassisted this pair turns up in 2.5% of games at mean turn 5.69 — and in 31.7% once a tutor is counted. The tutor is the line.
captions.Walking Ballista: **THE THREE-CARD KILL:** under Mikaeus a counterless Ballista is a 1/1 rather than a 0/0, so it needs an outside free outlet — and then it is unbounded damage with no drain payoff at all.

departments.pull_quote: A Snake token sacrificed under Mikaeus ceases to exist before its own undying trigger ever reaches the stack. Nothing comes back.
departments.note: Only stack 001 has passed the checker. No Blowfly, Ivy Lane, Scurry Oak or Host of the Hereafter line may appear in this section, and no altar pairing may be presented as a kill anywhere in the issue.

departments.headline: STAY BORING ON PURPOSE
departments.dek: Three opponents look at a 2/2 legend and two 1/1 tokens and file you under snake deck. That read is the most valuable thing you own — here is exactly what spends it.

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: You flip to archenemy the moment a drain converter that hits every seat lands beside a repeatable counter source. Hold the converter in hand for that turn rather than deploying it early to be shot off the table.

callouts.title: THE ELEVEN TELLS
callouts.text: Eleven Game Changers sit in this 99. The turn a Mox, a Demonic Tutor or The One Ring resolves, your Snakes stop reading as chump blockers.

callouts.title: SELL THE REAL NUMBER
callouts.text: In a Rule 0 conversation, say bracket 4, eleven Game Changers, one signed line. That honesty buys you a seat the bigger number would have cost.

pilot_tips.text: Put Yawgmoth down with a second body already on board and a turn that converts — anything less spends your scarcest card for one activation.

captions.The One Ring: **THE LOUDEST CARD HERE:** cast it for the cards, on a turn you can afford both the life and the attention — never as a protection turn you are hoping nobody prices.

departments.pull_quote: Three opponents will hold up mana against nineteen infinites the record credits you with exactly one of. Spend that discount on every value turn in between.

departments.headline: ONE CLASS OF FIVE
departments.dek: Fourteen interactive copies, and every one of them points at a creature. Sort each table by the permanent type that beats you and you will know before turn one which seats you answer and which you have to race.

threats.read: Your interaction covers exactly one permanent class, and it is not theirs. A resolved Sphere, Orb or hoser stays resolved, so believe that the turn it lands and stop burning turns hunting an answer you did not pack. Two things genuinely favour you: your engines cost no mana once assembled, and your commander lands on turn two, so you are often under the lock before its second and third pieces layer. Then trade with the truth — say out loud that you have no answer, and ask the seat holding the removal to spend it.

You can only interact with a creature-based kill, and against combo a held answer rots — the last profitable moment is now. Do not plan to out-race a dedicated combo deck either: the pairing you are most likely to reach turns up in 16.3% of games at mean turn 4.10 and nobody has adjudicated it. Be the seat their interaction is not pointed at, and remember how fast your Game Changers spend that cover.

Your token half is nearly free to lose. Bitterblossom rebuilds every upkeep, Skullclamp and Grim Haruspex cash the deaths, and a wrath with Blood Artist out is a drain you get to aim. The asymmetry runs the other way for your ceiling, though — Hapatra, Yawgmoth, Devoted Druid and Necroskitter are all creatures, so deploy in waves, lead with the half you do not mind losing, and hold the enabler until your window.

A board of 1/1s reads as free damage to them and is a wall of deathtouch to you: it blanks an attacker of any size, and one board answering three attack plans is advantage no removal count will ever show. Keep the Snakes home. Spend life on purpose here rather than by accident, because your engine bills the same total the painlands do.

The seat this deck was built for, and the only matchup where your one covered class is the right one. Their removal is poor against tokens and their attacks are poor into deathtouch. Hold single-target removal until something is pointed at you, land Crumbling Ashes early and let it grind, then win on cards rather than combat.

departments.pull_quote: Graveyard hate aimed at you costs three cards and nothing else. Let the seat that spent one on you feel good about it.

departments.headline: EIGHT TUTORS, ONE ANSWER
departments.dek: Eight tutors make the table think you can find anything. You can find one thing that matters, and the first wish nearly always has the same name.

pilot_tips.text: Fire it on the end step before your untap — a card put on top of your library is an appointment, not an arrival.
This is the only tutor here that puts a body straight onto the battlefield, and it shuffles itself back in — spend it early without agonising.

captions.Demonic Tutor: **THE DEFAULT WISH:** point it at a repeatable -1/-1 source. The converter class is four deep and turns up on its own in 51.9% of games.
captions.Survival of the Fittest: **ALMOST FREE HERE:** the discard costs you nothing once Phyrexian Reclamation can buy the creature back out of your graveyard.

departments.pull_quote: Never send a tutor after an altar to loop with Mikaeus. The record checked all five, and each one buys exactly one undying return.

departments.headline: NOTHING ENTERS TAPPED
departments.dek: Twenty-nine black sources and twenty-nine green from lands alone, against a target of twenty-two apiece — cleared before a single rock is counted. The invoice on this mana base is not colour. It is your life total.

pilot_tips.text: Lead on a basic while a painland can still wait — your engine bills the same life total that City of Brass, Mana Confluence and Tarnished Citadel do.

captions.Grim Monolith: **BUYING TURNS, NOT COLOURS:** it scores zero coloured sources under the unconditional-mana rule, alongside Sol Ring, Mana Vault and Chrome Mox.
captions.Forbidden Orchard: **THE ONE THAT PAYS THEM:** every tap hands an opponent a Spirit. That is a body your removal has to answer, so tap it when the counter is already spoken for.

departments.pull_quote: Black asks for 71.4% of the pips and holds half of the sources. It costs nothing here, because twenty-two of these lands answer either question.

departments.headline: THE MEDIAN IS THE PLAN
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded runs, one seed, no opponents. They measure how fast this deck develops — and they are blunt about which of its two plans actually turns up.

callouts.title: THE COMMANDER IS A CONSTANT
callouts.text: Turn two in 9,970 of 10,000 runs, mean cast turn 2.007. Stop deliberating over turn two and move that thinking to turn three.

callouts.title: THE MEDIAN GAME
callouts.text: Your commander plus a payoff, 67.2% of games at mean turn 3.62. A drain converter, 51.9%. That is the deck you are actually piloting.

callouts.title: THE CEILING
callouts.text: Mikaeus plus Devoted Druid: 2.5% assembled, 1.3% by turn six, mean turn 5.69 — and 31.7% once a tutor is counted. Pace for the median and take the ceiling when it is handed to you.

callouts.title: WHAT THIS IS NOT
callouts.text: No opponents, no removal, no interaction, and no credit for cost reducers or extra draw. A simulation of resource development is not a prediction of a game.

departments.pull_quote: One game in forty on your own; roughly one in three once a tutor is counted. That gap is the whole difference between a plan and a hope.

departments.headline: TWO CARDS FIX THE NUMBER
departments.dek: One permanent class answered out of five is the figure that decides your hard matchups. Two picks below take it to five of five — and most of the rest go to the thinnest part of the engine.

pilot_tips.text: Read the cut beside each pick, not just the pick: Crumbling Ashes only ever kills a creature, and creatures are the one class you already answer.

captions.Blowfly Infestation: **THE ONE WITH NO CLOSER:** a pass across 11,799 green-black cards found nothing that repeats what it does. Some thin spots simply stay thin.

departments.pull_quote: Ramp is the only axis over target, and that is where half these cuts come from. Nothing on this list buys mana or generic draw.

departments.headline: ONE CASE, FOUR PASSES
departments.dek: The complete record behind every ✓ in this issue: the question put to it, every step, and each rule quoted in full. Open the file and check us.
departments.pull_quote: The clause that decides this case is inside undying itself: return it if it had no +1/+1 counters on it.

departments.headline: EIGHTY PAIRS OF HANDS
departments.dek: Eighty artists share these 88 cards and nobody holds more than three. There is no signature on this deck — so the story is the breadth, and how little of it anyone actually chose.

featured.note:
Daniel Ljunggren leads this roster with three cards, and in an eighty-artist field that is not a signature. It is the crest of a very flat wave. John Avon also has three. Nobody else clears two.

Say plainly why it is flat. The decklist names cards and not editions, so each entry carries whatever printing came back for the name. The largest single stamp on the deck is one Commander product holding twelve cards by twelve different artists, and there is not a single foil among the 88. No taste was exercised here, and we are not going to invent some.

What chance handed over is still worth the page. Ljunggren's three are Black Sun's Zenith, Forbidden Orchard and Walking Ballista — the sweeper the whole economy runs through, the land that hands your opponents Spirits, and the piece the case file affirmed as a real kill. For a flat field, that is a good crest.

also_worth_noting.note: Opal Palace and Spire of Industry are classic Avon architecture. Serrated Arrows is the odd one out — even the removal slot gets a landscape painter here.
Two cards, maximum gravity: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed, the hinge of this whole issue, and Eternal Witness, the rebuy that keeps the engine honest.
Chrome Mox and Worldly Tutor — two of the eleven Game Changers, one brush.

captions.Black Sun's Zenith: **THE SIGNATURE PIECE:** X counters on each creature is one placement event, and this deck reads it as a wipe, a Snake wave and a mass reanimation at once.

departments.note: Counts are recomputed by the renderer from artist-credits and are per entry throughout. Forest and Swamp are one entry each at seven copies — counting per copy would push two basic-land painters to the top of a roster they do not lead.

rhythm_notes: The arc is the spec's five acts and I changed nothing in it. Act I opens instructional and lands on The 99, which is browsing — a deliberate soft landing before Act II asks for work. Act II climbs practice to participation to the peak: The Kill closes the act as the payoff to meeting the deck and learning to fly it, and it reads as narrative even though it carries the technical content. Act III is three straight Coach sections and I kept Know Your Enemy's threat boxes as the reference beat between two instructional ones, so reflection, reference and instruction alternate inside a single voice. Act IV is the only place two dense analysis spreads sit together, and the renderer's declared art break after Sources Say is the breather — I added no furniture there. The Short List is deliberately low-intensity imagination after it, and Judge's Desk is buffered by imagination before and appreciation after, exactly as the table wants. The two peaks (cover, The Kill) are the only places I let violators and full-bleed treatment run.
gaps: manual_prose.json's `upgrades` body names a different ten than considering.json — Beast Within, Nature's Claim, Scavenging Ooze, Forsaken Miner, The Great Henge, Peer into the Abyss and Triskelion, against a list whose ten are Assassin's Trophy, Dawnhand Dissident, Sinister Gnarlbark, Evolution Sage, Gravecrawler, Boseiju Who Endures, Poison-Tip Archer, Reassembling Skeleton, Persistent Constrictor and The Meathook Massacre. The renderer prints that prose immediately above the rendered ten, so a reader sees two different lists on one page. My copy for the section is written against considering.json only; the prose needs a rewrite I am not scoped for.

One checker-passed stack for a deck holding 32 contained combo lines. The single highest-value scenario is whether Mikaeus's anthem switches the Blowfly and Hapatra token loops off — under a +1/+1 anthem a 1/1 token survives one -1/-1 counter, which would make the deck's two headline engines mutually exclusive on the battlefield. Nothing else changes sequencing this much.

Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation is the pairing the pilot actually reaches — 16.3% assembled, 12.5% by turn six — and it has never had a scenario. Until it does, every section here treats Blowfly as a counter source and nothing more, which costs the issue its most likely kill spread.

Yawgmoth plus Hapatra without Mikaeus is plausibly the line this deck wins with most often and is unresolved: the fizzle rule, the target-survives requirement and the life and library bounds all need settling before The Kill can carry it.

The strategy DB has no section on auditing a combo list — how to price an unverified combo count, why pairwise combo data drops third pieces, and what a verified-kill count should do to a Rule 0 conversation. That idea is the spine of this issue and every sentence of it had to be derived from the deck's own artifacts.

No aristocrats or counters-matter section in the strategy DB either: the outlet / fodder / converter taxonomy, free versus costed outlets, each-opponent versus single-target drains, and the anthem-versus-shrink anti-synergy are all load-bearing here and all derived from oracle text.

No deck_recon.json for this commander, so nothing in The Short List is grounded in what other Hapatra lists actually run — inclusion rates would settle whether a one-of-five interaction suite is normal for this deck or an outlier.
